comment.comment: A '#' opens a comment everywhere EXCEPT immediately after a facade name, where it reaches a constant. #scoped-call matches at the '@', which is earlier, and the earliest match wins — so `@player#MAX` is a constant access and `# a note` is a comment, without either rule having to know about the other.
comment.name: comment.line.number-sign.jmx

behaviour-block.comment: Both spellings, because the backend's lexer accepts both and a file refused over a 'u' is a file nobody enjoys.

on-handler.comment: The event name is whatever word follows 'on', INCLUDING one spelled like a keyword — a host is entitled to an event called 'end'. The optional literal of `on timer 180` falls through to #expression.

function-block.comment: `function share(count : int, total : int) : double` — each parameter may carry a type, and the function its result's after the closing parenthesis.

declaration.comment: `let count : int = 1`, `local` (the same word), `const limit = 10`; `state hits : int = 0` and `parameter limit = 10` only where they open a declaration — a name, then `:` or `=` — because a host hands its scripts a plain `state` (`when state == 'FAILED'`). The type gets a scope of its own — entity.name.type — so it stands apart from names and keywords in every theme.

keyword.comment: Control words only. `and`, `or`, `not`, `is` and `in` are OPERATORS in this language and live in #operator-word — `not` in particular is the engine's second spelling of `!=` and the partner of `is`, never a prefix. Negation is `!`. Declarations are #declaration.
keyword.name: keyword.control.jmx

scoped-call.comment: Existing jME: @bean.method(args) | @bean#CONST | @bean:$field. The one syntax in a script that reaches outside it, so it is coloured as a thing of its own.

assignment.comment: A lone '=' assigns; '==' compares, and writing the second where the first was meant is refused at load — it would otherwise evaluate and throw its answer away. They are one token type to the lexer, so they are told apart here by what surrounds them, and coloured apart because that is the mistake this language expects people to make.
assignment.name: keyword.operator.assignment.jmx

long-text.comment: ExperienceNotation: """ … """ spans lines and is markdown; it must be tried before a one-line string.
long-text.name: string.quoted.triple.jmx

document.comment: kind "Title" [as slug] [type role] { … }: a kind's word followed by a quoted title. Only `set` may hold documents, but every body includes this rule so a nested one is coloured as a document rather than as noise.
document.name: meta.document.jmx

symbol-document.comment: A symbol document's body is a drawing written without the braces of a symbol block: size, path, pin, label.
symbol-document.name: meta.document.symbol.jmx

header-line.comment: Kind.DECLARATIONS — extends ref, use a, b and units A, B: top-level lines that change what the document computes.

patterns.comment: type power_density = power / area: a quantity the document names; every word in it is a type.
patterns.name: meta.line.type.jmx

patterns.comment: The fields the reader knows and checks.
Any other field: 'name value', kept with its type.
x in …, or (z) / (x, y) for a plane.
name [: type] then = expression, where equation, a description or nothing.
let I_through : current = … — `local` is the same word; the type, when written, stands apart (entity.name.type).
d(x)/dt = …
current a -> b = … and voltage a -> b = …: a branch from one pin to another.
x_next = … and x_start = …
0 = …: an implicit equation.

figure-unit.comment: display/measure: `unit %`, `unit V`, `unit A/V^2` after the expression.

patterns.comment: plus red stripes black: a pin, its lead's colour, and its stripes'.
f(u, v) = …: a jMF definition.

script-braces.comment: A brace inside a jMS body is jMS's, so it must not close the block.

patterns.name: meta.block.preset.jmx
patterns.comment: preset "Title" ["what it shows"] { name = value, … }
Anything else is a representation: its name, primary, then its settings as written.

symbol-uses.comment: symbol uses diode-symbol[, other] [{ a anode; b cathode }]: the symbols that draw the component, the first the default, and the port each pin lands on.

patterns.comment: closed = pressed: what one of the symbol's inputs is drawn from, an expression over the part.

symbol-shape.comment: symbol box { left d, clk edge; right q }: a shape or a glyph, its pins placed by side or by the glyph's ports.
symbol-shape.name: meta.block.symbol.jmx

drawing.comment: size W x H, path "…", pin NAME at x, y ["label"], label NAME at x, y — and a living drawing: input NAME [range], elements with properties, live when layers, hide.

living-layer.comment: live when <condition> { … }: a layer drawn while its condition on the inputs holds.
living-layer.name: meta.block.living-layer.jmx

living-element-block.comment: [live] path|box|circle|line|group [name] [placing] { properties and elements }: an element with braces of its own.
living-element-block.name: meta.block.living-element.jmx

living-property.comment: [live|animate] rotate = between(-30 deg, 0 deg, closed): a property, marked as it changes, and its value in jMF.

part-line.comment: ID reference [unit U] (connections) [settings] [place x, y [rotate deg] [mirror]]: parts, internals and benches alike.

patterns.comment: PART.pin at a wire's ends: R1.positive, V1.+, Ja.j.
CH1 out [against reference] 2 V/div, M1 voltage p, M2 current PS1.negative rms, M3 power RL, L1 level clock: what is measured, by its own name.
clock t [from a to b] [speed s] [loop]: the parameter it moves comes first.
a circuit pane plays a circuit: uses <slug> [over a .. b].
Every line opens with its name.
What follows the expression, in this order: until u, at (x, y), in pane, color n, hidden.
A label: a text whose {…} parts are read live.
patterns.name: string.quoted.label.jmx

patterns.comment: weight : (x expression, y expression)

instrument-line.comment: An instrument's objects, representations and the object it opens: objects geometric_construction, point_set.
instrument-line.name: meta.line.instrument.jmx

collection-section.comment: section "Ordinary" { items … }: a collection's section and its items.
collection-section.name: meta.block.section.jmx

course-lesson.comment: lesson "Title" [as slug] { summary …; minutes 10; object …; step "…" { … } }
course-lesson.name: meta.block.lesson.jmx

assignments.comment: name = value, separated by commas or not: a part's settings, a preset, a turtle.

circuit-function.comment: d(q)/dt in an equation; a pin's members — anode.current, anode.voltage — anywhere a formula is; current and level in a measurement. A pin's bare name is its voltage, so it needs nothing.

quantity.comment: Quantity.java: a number and the unit written after it — 2.52 nA, 0.3 V/us, 10 kOhm, A/V^2, 1/s, 5%, 90 deg. A unit is one token with its number; '2 C' is two coulombs, not 2·C.

imaginary.comment: -0.8 + 0.156 i: the imaginary unit after a number.

formula.comment: A jMF expression: numbers with units, ranges, tolerances, calls, constants and operators.
